The home mountain of the Greek Gods is Mount Olympus.

To understand how search engines work, imagine the Internet as a massive, chaotic library that never stops growing. In this library, every website is a book, and every web page is a single page within that book. If you were looking for a specific fact, you wouldn't want to read every book from cover to cover. Instead, you would use the library's index or catalog system to find the exact book and page that contains your answer. Search engines like Google act as this intelligent index. They crawl the "library" of the Internet, cataloging the "books" (websites) and "pages" (web pages), so that when you ask a question, they can instantly point you to the most relevant source, saving you from having to search through millions of pages manually.
